workstream.name: ecl v1 — the real interpreter (design/workstream-v1.md)
workstream.unlocks: User-authored native extensions loaded from ECL_PATH, and M10's CSV and JSON modules as first-party consumers of the same typed callback and capability protocol — which is exactly the capability set this milestone ships. It also fixes the shape of the additive future capabilities it deliberately defers: module state with view/update authority, Offload, resources, external wake, package assets, and quotation evaluation.

problemStatement: Stock `ecl` cannot load precompiled native code at all. The only native seam is `Session.registerNativeModule` (session.zig:554) feeding `modules.registerNative` (modules.zig:1377), whose callbacks receive `machine.NativeMachine` — the whole operand stack plus an allocator — and which is reachable only from in-process Zig test code. There is no artifact, no ABI, no capability contract, no scheduler budget, and no lifetime, so a callback can pop arbitrary operands, block a worker forever, and leave a half-mutated stack behind on failure. M10's CSV and JSON modules and every user-authored accelerator need a real trusted extension boundary before they can be written, and the current seam would have to be an authority bypass to serve them. This milestone builds exactly the capability set those two modules consume and no more.
solutionSummary: Freeze a C-shaped ABI-v1 wire contract in one file shared by the runtime and a new `ecl-native` Zig SDK whose module-root directory makes importing interpreter internals a compile error. The SDK derives each word's effect, arity, and capability manifest at comptime from one `*ecl.Call("inputs -- outputs")` first parameter and emits one descriptor plus one uniform adapter behind one entry symbol, so authors write no requirements list, callback table, or allocator plumbing. The runtime validates and copies every descriptor field through bounded cursors before it initializes module state or publishes anything, then drives each native word as a transaction that pins its inputs and reserves the exact final stack window before committing. `ECL_PATH` gains `<name>.eclmod` as the second candidate inside each root, resolved source-first and fail-closed on the first existing candidate. Cooperation is a typed `Reschedule` continuation running on the production `machine.WorkDriver` path with the ordinary 65,536-unit budget. The v1 capability set is closed at exactly what M10's CSV and JSON modules consume — `Call`, `BuildValues`, `Reschedule` — with module state, `Offload`, resources, external wake, package assets, and quotation evaluation deferred behind reserved ids.

operationalConsiderations.externalSystemAccess: The one new external dependency is the host dynamic loader. The runtime executing the new code is the `ecl` process itself; today it reaches the filesystem only through `std.Io.Dir.cwd().access`/read in `AutoLoadDriver` and `FileSourceDriver`, with `ECL_PATH` supplied by `src/main.zig` (main.zig:181, 216) and stored on `SessionCore.ecl_path`. Patch 5 adds `std.DynLib.openZ` + `lookup(abi.EntryFn, "ecl_module_abi_v1")` + `close` on Linux and macOS, owned entirely by `src/native_module.zig`; no network, database, queue, secret store, or new credential is involved, and no new environment variable is introduced. Opening a library is arbitrary trusted-code execution — platform constructors can run before ECL sees the descriptor — so the access posture is stated rather than mitigated: a native-bearing `ECL_PATH` is a trusted dependency path, the loader error text says so, and Patch 7's README makes it the headline of the trust guide. On a target where `std.DynLib` is unsupported, an existing `.eclmod` candidate is still authoritative and fails with a precise `'io` error rather than silently falling through to a later candidate. No `*Client`/`*Transport` indirection is introduced: `ModuleInstance` is a nominal handle over a real image, not a sentinel for missing access.
operationalConsiderations.crossRuntimeContracts: The `.eclmod` descriptor is a genuine cross-runtime contract between two separately compiled binaries. The producer is an author's extension built against the `ecl-native` SDK; the consumer is the `ecl` runtime's validator and loader. Both sides are patched in this gameplan and both read their layouts from the single shared file `src/native/abi.zig` — that file is the contract, and Rule 3's shared anchor for every name in it. Compatibility is versioned explicitly: ABI major must match exactly, minor is additive, every record carries its own byte size, readers take `@min(declared, @sizeOf(local))`, and unknown trailing bytes are ignored, so an older v1 artifact keeps loading on a newer v1 runtime whenever every capability it names is supported. Patches 6 and 7 extend the wire table by additive tails and bump `abi_minor` rather than reshaping records. A breaking change requires ABI v2, which v1 does not ship. The C-shaped encoding is deliberately not a supported C author API in v1: no Zig slice, error union, enum layout, tagged union, allocator, or author type crosses the boundary, so the binary promise stays narrow enough to keep. The second contract is the artifact filename convention `<module>.eclmod` on `ECL_PATH`, produced by `installExtension` and consumed by `AutoLoadDriver`; both sides land in this gameplan and the acceptance suite exercises the pair end to end.
operationalConsiderations.failureBehavior: Every native failure class has a named disposition. Descriptor defects (ABI major mismatch, unsupported capability id or version, short/oversized record, count or offset overflow, out-of-range callback index, invalid UTF-8, empty documentation, unparseable effect, duplicate word, nonzero reserved state layout, name mismatch) are rejected by `native_descriptor.ValidateCursor` before any state initialization or publication, each with its own error and failing definition index; the cursor retires its own partial materializations on the failure path. Load-time host errors — file unreadable, `dlopen` failure, missing entry symbol, unsupported platform — are `'io` errors naming the candidate path, and the first existing candidate is authoritative, so a broken artifact is never silently skipped. At call time, deliberate failure, cancellation, deadline loss, OOM, and abandonment all leave the operand stack byte-identical and transfer tentative candidates to `heap.ReleaseDomain` retirement. Native authors may name only the eight permitted kinds with a bounded message; underflow, undefined-word, contract, cancellation, timeout, and OOM stay runtime-owned. The one failure this gameplan deliberately does not handle is a native callback that ignores the cooperative contract: machine code cannot be preempted, so a runaway or blocking callback stalls its worker and is only reported after the fact by the duration/overrun diagnostic. That limit is documented in the README and demonstrated by a deliberately non-cooperative fixture, so it is a stated boundary rather than an unnoticed hazard. External side effects a native word performs are explicitly outside operand-stack rollback.
operationalConsiderations.concurrencyAndIdempotency: Every new path is entered concurrently. Loading is serialized by the existing `modules.Registry.beginLoadingCursor` `LoadingLease`, which already prevents recursive and concurrent auto-load of the same name, and publication goes through the existing `createCandidate`/`commit` protocol, so a native module competes for its registry slot exactly like a source module and a mid-table failure rolls the whole candidate back. `ModuleInstance` is created once per Session under `Session`'s `BlockingMutationTurn`, so registration and retirement settlement stay coupled. This milestone deliberately adds no new scheduler wait-set variant: with module state deferred, a native call never blocks on a shared resource, so the only suspension it can cause is the ordinary cooperative yield already served by `machine.WorkDriver`. Native calls are not idempotent and are not retried by the runtime: a call runs once, and a yield resumes the same continuation rather than restarting it. The continuation is consumed exactly once by `complete`/`fail`/`cancel` and its bounded destructor runs exactly once. Ordering of native side effects is the author's responsibility and is stated as such.
operationalConsiderations.rollbackStrategy: Two stateful surfaces exist. First, the operand stack: the transaction is the rollback mechanism — inputs are pinned and never mutated until `Machine.reserveStack` has secured the exact final window, so every non-completing exit is a no-op on the stack by construction rather than by compensating writes. Second, any external effect a native word performs: it is explicitly outside operand-stack rollback, documented beside the rollback code and in the README, because the runtime cannot know how to undo them. At the artifact level, publication is all-or-nothing through the existing candidate protocol, so a failed load leaves no partial registry entry to clean up. Reverting a patch of this gameplan is a pure code revert: no schema, no migration, no persisted format, and no on-disk state is created by the interpreter — the only durable artifacts are `.eclmod` files an author or CI builds, which are regenerated by `zig build native-fixture` and are not read by any earlier `ecl` version (an ecl without native support simply never looks for `.eclmod`, so an installed artifact is inert rather than corrupting). The one asymmetry worth naming: Patch 4 deletes the public `Session.registerNativeModule` API, and reverting Patches 5-7 without also reverting Patch 4 would leave the tree with no native registration surface at all — which is why the gameplan is atomic and reverts as a unit.

mergabilityStrategy.featureFlagStrategy: Ship ungated, and this is a decision rather than a default: the repository has no flag service and no flag table, its only runtime switches are `ECL_WORKERS` (parsed in src/main.zig) and the `session_options.default_worker_count` build option, and M7 explicitly ruled that scheduler configuration is not a rollout flag. Native loading changes nothing until an operator places a `.eclmod` on `ECL_PATH`, so the artifact's presence is already the opt-in and a second toggle would only create a state where a trusted, installed dependency silently does not load. The security posture is handled by fail-closed descriptor validation, the loader's precise error text, and the README trust guide, not by a kill switch. Confirmed with the programmer during gameplan review: no env var and no build option gates native loading, so there is exactly one resolution mode for the acceptance matrix to cover.
mergabilityStrategy.patchOrderingStrategy: Patch 1 is pure constants, documentation, and a dependency-free wire-contract file — no behavior. Patches 2 and 3 build the validator and the SDK behind that contract, still with no runtime reachability. Patch 4 runs parallel to them and only deletes the retired seam. Patch 5 is the first observable behavior: an artifact loads and a native word runs. Patch 6 adds cooperation and ordered teardown on the same instance and transaction types. Patch 7 is acceptance, CI, documentation, and the final audit sync. Four of seven patches are INFRA and the three behavioral patches are ordered smallest-blast-radius first.

DESIGN.md carries a d.21 addendum reconciling trusted `.eclmod` dependencies with the positioning: no machine code is generated by ecl, core and stdlib stay a single binary, `.eclmod` artifacts are optional installed dependencies on an explicitly trusted path, and d.9's cached compiled form still means threaded or opcode arrays only.

Descriptor metadata is rejected before any observable effect: an artifact with a wrong ABI major, an unsupported capability id/version, a short or oversized record, an out-of-range count/index/callback index, invalid UTF-8, empty documentation, a malformed effect, a duplicate word name, an out-of-range state size/alignment, or a name that differs from the requested module produces a precise failure and initializes no state.

`zig build native-fixture` produces a loadable `sample.eclmod` from the `ecl-native` SDK without rebuilding or relinking `ecl`, and `zig build test-native-sdk-negative` fails compilation for a callback that lacks the `*ecl.Call("in -- out")` first parameter, returns the wrong type, is generic, declares a malformed effect, names an unknown capability, duplicates a word, omits documentation, or returns the wrong output arity.

The general-stack native seam is gone: `Session.registerNativeModule`, `modules.registerNative`'s `NativeDefinition` list, `env.Primitive`/`PrimitiveOutcome`/`PrimitiveResult`, the `Binding.primitive` variant, and `machine.NativeMachine` no longer exist, so no callback can obtain the whole operand stack or an allocator.

`use` of an unregistered module tries `<name>.ecl` and then `<name>.eclmod` inside each `ECL_PATH` entry in order; the first existing candidate is authoritative including its failures, so a broken first candidate never falls through to a later candidate or a later path root.

A validated `.eclmod` publishes its complete word table atomically and pins its code image for the Session; its words are callable qualified, through `use`, and through `alias`, and appear in `words` and REPL completion exactly like source-module exports.

`doc` returns a native word's documentation, and `which` and `see` additionally report that the binding is native and list the artifact's inferred capability requirements alongside the ordinary effect and generation.

A native word is a transactional leaf call: its declared inputs stay pinned and immutable for the whole call, only exact completion replaces exactly those inputs with exactly the declared outputs, and deliberate failure, cancellation, deadline loss, OOM, or abandonment leaves the operand stack byte-identical while every tentative candidate value goes to bounded retirement.

A native failure may name only `type`, `shape`, `conform`, `overflow`, `domain`, `parse`, `io`, or `user` with a bounded message; underflow, undefined-word, contract, cancellation, timeout, and OOM plus all word/source/trace attachment remain runtime-owned and are attached to the native error dict by the runtime.

A first-party statically linked module publishes its SDK-generated descriptor through a private static transport with a no-op image pin, taking the identical validation, publication, transaction, reflection, and shutdown path as a dynamically loaded artifact; the transport is not a Session method and accepts no library handle, so no ECL-in-Zig embedding API is exposed.

A cooperative native word advances on the production scheduler path: aggregate observation and construction charge the same 65,536-unit budget as first-party kernels, exhaustion yields with inputs, candidates, and typed continuation intact, cancellation is observed within one native quantum, and other ready units make progress between slices even with one worker.

With `ECL_NATIVE_DIAGNOSTICS` set, a native invocation that exceeds its quantum without cooperating produces a rate-limited per-module duration/overrun diagnostic on the Session diagnostics stream instead of being preempted; with the variable unset the runtime samples no clock and emits nothing, and neither mode preempts.

Session shutdown closes new native-call creation, joins and cancels tasks, destroys every call continuation, settles ECL retirement, and only then closes the code image, so no callback can run after the image closes even when a delayed continuation was alive at shutdown.

The README gains the native-extension guide: how to depend on the `ecl-native` SDK, how to build a `.eclmod` for a target, and the explicit statement that a native-bearing `ECL_PATH` is a trusted-code path because opening a library executes arbitrary code before ECL can inspect the descriptor.

CI blocks on the native gates: `native-fixture`, `test-native-sdk-negative`, `test-native-runtime` at Debug and ReleaseSafe, `fuzz-native-descriptor`, `fuzz-native-call`, the one-and-eight-worker native runtime matrix, the native TSan filter, and the extended `test-oom` probe.

explicitOpinions.opinion: DESIGN.md gains a d.21 addendum rather than a new numbered decision or no ledger entry at all.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Programmer ruling during gameplan review. d.21 currently reads `interpreted forever — no JIT, no machine-code compilation, ever` plus a single-binary positioning, so a reader of the ledger alone would conclude that loading `.eclmod` artifacts contradicts it; the reconciliation belongs where that reader is. An addendum rather than d.24 keeps the settled-decision count stable and matches the fact that most of the native boundary is architecture rather than semantics — it stays in ARCHITECTURE.md, and the ledger records only what the positioning promise does and does not cover.

explicitOpinions.opinion: M9 ships exactly the capability set M10's CSV and JSON modules consume — mandatory `Call` plus optional `BuildValues` and `Reschedule` — and defers `ModuleState`, `ModuleView`, and `ModuleUpdate` with their scheduler-integrated arbiter to a later milestone.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Programmer directive during gameplan review: scope this milestone narrowly to what CSV and JSON need. Both modules are pure value-in/value-out transforms with no per-Session state, so the arbiter, the `ParkRequest.native_state` wait-set variant, the state-embedding comptime validation, and four compile-negative fixtures were all speculative. Removing them deletes the riskiest piece of the milestone — a new scheduler wait-set variant — drops the native component ceiling from 4,000 to 3,000 and the total from 37,000 to 36,000, and removes one whole patch. The deferral is made unreachable rather than half-present: `module_view` and `module_update` stay reserved capability ids with no supported version and the descriptor's `StateLayout` must be zero, so an artifact naming them is refused at load while the additive-tail rule keeps ABI v1 open for the real capability later. The follow-on work is proposed back to the workstream as its own milestone rather than being dropped.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The per-invocation native duration/overrun diagnostic is opt-in through `ECL_NATIVE_DIAGNOSTICS` and silent by default: with the variable unset no clock is sampled and no counter is touched.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Programmer ruling during gameplan review, chosen over always-on counters and an always-on stderr line. It keeps the default path free of both measurement cost and stderr noise for legitimately slow leaf words. The tension it creates was raised and accepted: the default build does not observe the non-preemption violation it documents, so DoD-23’s clause and the README must say the observability is opt-in, and the acceptance suite runs the non-cooperative fixture in both modes so the off case is a tested behavior rather than an untested absence.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Native extension loading ships ungated — no feature flag, no opt-in environment variable, and no build option that compiles the loader out.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Resolved with the programmer during gameplan review. Placing a `.eclmod` on `ECL_PATH` is already a deliberate operator act, so a second toggle would only add a state where an installed trusted dependency silently fails to load, which reads as a defect rather than a safeguard. It would also fork every DoD-22/23/24 fixture run into two resolution modes and, in the build-option variant, fork the source-audit component measurement. The trust boundary is addressed where it is real: fail-closed validation before any side effect, a load error that names arbitrary-code execution, and the README guide.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The private static transport lands in Patch 5 as a second image-pin arm of the same load typestate, and is proved in this milestone by registering the real SDK fixture as a statically linked Zig module.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Resolved with the programmer during gameplan review. Shipping the arm unexercised would violate AGENTS.md's rule that a type declaration compiling without any caller is not proof its public surface works, and deferring it to M10 would force M10's first patch to reopen the loader typestate. Modelling it as an image-pin variant rather than a parallel path guarantees static and dynamic registration cannot diverge in validation, publication, transaction, or teardown — the divergence is exactly one field.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The author-facing SDK lives at `src/native/` and is exposed as the build module `ecl-native` rooted at `src/native/sdk.zig`, rather than in a separate repository.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Zig forbids importing a file above a module's root directory, so rooting the module at `src/native/sdk.zig` makes `@import("../machine.zig")` a compile error. That is a compiler-enforced boundary rather than a source denylist, which is exactly what AGENTS.md asks for ('Enforce a repository rule in the type system, then the audit, then nowhere'). A separate repository would add a release-synchronization problem without adding any enforcement, and `build.zig.zon`'s existing `.paths` already ships `src`, so consumers can depend on this repo directly.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The dependency chain is deliberately near-linear: only the {2,3} SDK/validator branch runs parallel to Patch 4's seam removal.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Patches 5 and 6 both extend the same three files (`native_module.zig`, `native_call.zig`, `native/capability.zig`) plus the same fixture, and two concurrent agents would each invent an incompatible continuation, capability, and teardown state machine. Patch 4 is genuinely disjoint — it only deletes from `env.zig`/`machine.zig`/`modules.zig`/`session.zig`/`definition_prims.zig`/`module_test.zig` — so it is the one branch worth running in parallel.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Patch 4 removes the old seam *before* Patch 5 introduces the new one, accepting a temporary window with no native binding variant at all.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Keeping both alive at once would leave `env.Binding` with two callback variants and force every switch, reflection path, and test to reason about which is authoritative — precisely the 'authority bypass' the workstream says must not survive. Deleting first makes the intermediate state coherent (bindings are word, value, builtin) and makes Patch 5's `.native` arm the only native path by construction. The three deleted tests' subject matter is re-established under the new transaction in the same gameplan, so no coverage is abandoned.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Capability types are introduced patch by patch (`Call`/`ValueView`/`BuildValues` in Patch 3, `Reschedule` in Patch 6) instead of declaring the whole set up front.
explicitOpinions.rationale: AGENTS.md is explicit that 'a type declaration compiling without any caller is not proof that its public surface works' and requires every operation of an opaque public capability to be exercised through its real registration or runtime path. Declaring the whole set in Patch 3 would ship capabilities unexercised for several patches. The capability *ids* are still reserved in the wire contract from Patch 1, so an artifact requesting an unimplemented capability gets a precise unsupported-version rejection rather than an unknown-id one.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The line-budget rebaseline installs the ceilings before any native code exists rather than ratcheting them per patch.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The workstream requires the remeasurement to happen 'before its first production patch', and a per-patch ratchet would make every later patch touch `src/tools/source_audit.zig`, ARCHITECTURE.md, and the workstream — three shared files that would serialize the whole gameplan and invite drift between the three authorities. Patch 7 re-measures and corrects the table once at the end, which is the only place the final numbers are knowable.

patches.title: Rebaseline the line-budget domain and freeze the ABI-v1 wire contract

files.description: The complete C-shaped ABI-v1 wire contract shared by the runtime and the SDK: entry symbol, version constants, sized extern records, capability ids, and result tags, with comptime layout assertions.
Export the wire contract as `native_abi` and reference it from the aggregate test block.
Add the `native SDK, ABI, and loader` component, raise the machine/modules/definition-annotation ceilings, and raise `business_logic_budget` to 36,000.
Replace the budget table with the remeasured figures plus the new component row, and record the `src/native/` module-root boundary.
Turn M9's remeasurement paragraph and DoD-33's ceilings into the installed record.
Add the d.21 addendum reconciling trusted .eclmod dependencies with the positioning.

changes: Create `src/native/abi.zig` as the sole wire contract. Declare `pub const entry_symbol = "ecl_module_abi_v1"`, `pub const abi_major: u32 = 1`, `pub const abi_minor: u32 = 0`, and `extern struct` records with fixed-width integers and explicit pointer/length pairs only: `Descriptor` (self `size: u32`, `abi_major`, `abi_minor`, module name ptr+len, module doc ptr+len, definition count + array ptr + per-record size, capability count + array ptr + per-record size, `StateLayout`, `HostTable` ptr+size), `Definition` (self size, name ptr+len, doc ptr+len, effect input count + input-name array, effect output count + output-name array, `callback_index: u32`), `CapabilityRequirement` (`id: u32`, `version: u32`), `StateLayout` (`size: u64`, `alignment: u32`, reserved for the deferred module-state capability and required to be zero in v1), `HostTable` (the runtime-provided function pointers the adapter calls), and `Invoke` (the artifact-provided per-definition entry). No Zig slice, error union, tagged union, `packed struct`, allocator, or author type may appear in this file — enforce that with a `comptime` walk over every declared record's fields that rejects any non-extern-compatible field type.

Freeze the negotiation rule in the same file: every record carries its own `size`, readers take `@min(record.size, @sizeOf(LocalRecord))`, unknown trailing bytes are ignored, ABI major must match exactly, and a differing minor is accepted. Document that a breaking representation or semantic change requires ABI v2. Add `comptime` `@sizeOf`/`@alignOf`/`@offsetOf` assertions for every record so a layout change fails the build instead of a test.

Declare the capability id space as a non-exhaustive `enum(u32)` with `call`, `build_values`, and `reschedule` supported in v1, plus `module_view` and `module_update` present as reserved ids with no supported version. Reserving the deferred ids costs two enum members and keeps the additive-tail rule usable when module state lands; an artifact naming a reserved id is rejected with a precise unsupported-capability error rather than an unknown-id error.

Declare the wire result tags: `CallResult = enum(u32) { complete, fail, yield }` and `ErrorKindWire = enum(u32)` with exactly the eight author-permitted members `type`, `shape`, `conform`, `overflow`, `domain`, `parse`, `io`, `user`, plus a `comptime` assertion that each maps onto a distinct `machine.ErrorKind` member. Perform that mapping check by name inside abi.zig without importing machine.zig, so the SDK build stays free of interpreter imports; the runtime side asserts the inverse direction in Patch 2.

Export the file from `src/root.zig` (`pub const native_abi = @import("native/abi.zig");`) and add `_ = native_abi;` to the aggregate `test` block so the comptime assertions are analyzed by `zig build test`.

In `src/tools/source_audit.zig` add a twelfth component `.{ .name = "native SDK, ABI, and loader", .budget = 3000, .files = &.{"native/abi.zig"}, .sources = &.{@embedFile("../native/abi.zig")} }`; raise `machine` 5,600 -> 5,900, `modules and registry` 4,800 -> 5,300, `definition annotations` 1,000 -> 1,100, and `business_logic_budget` 30,000 -> 36,000. Leave `scheduler and concurrency` at 3,500 and every other ceiling unchanged: with module-state arbitration deferred, this milestone adds no scheduler wait-set variant. Verify that `sameSourcePath` already matches the nested `native/abi.zig` walker path and that no other change to the coverage sweep is needed.

Run `zig build source-audit` and copy its per-component measured numbers verbatim into ARCHITECTURE.md's table (currently lines 30-43), adding the new component row and the new 36,000 total. Replace the paragraph at lines 68-82 that says the 30,000 ceiling remains authoritative with the executed record of this rebaseline, and extend the source-layout paragraph at lines 64-66 to state that `src/native/` holds the author-facing SDK package whose module-root directory is what makes importing interpreter internals a compile error. If a measured component now exceeds the ceiling proposed here, raise that ceiling and say why in the same edit rather than compressing a type boundary.

The workstream's planning envelope was 4,000 native lines and 37,000 total on the assumption that module-state arbitration landed in M9. It does not: the v1 capability set is closed at `Call`, `BuildValues`, and `Reschedule`, which is exactly what M10's CSV and JSON modules consume. Install 3,000 and 36,000 instead and record that reason in ARCHITECTURE.md, in M9's workstream section, and in DoD-33's assertion text, so all three authorities carry the same numbers and the same justification.

Update `design/workstream-v1.md` in the same change: M9's closing remeasurement paragraph becomes the record of what was installed, DoD-33's assertion text names the same numbers as ARCHITECTURE.md and the audit constants, and M9's Definition of Done records the narrowed capability set with module state deferred.

Add a d.21 addendum to `design/DESIGN.md` (the decision runs from line 444), in the same voice as the existing sub-bullets. It must say four things: ecl still generates no machine code, so `interpreted forever` is untouched; core and stdlib remain a single binary and `.eclmod` artifacts are optional installed dependencies, never required runtime pieces; a native-bearing `ECL_PATH` is an explicitly trusted dependency path because opening a library executes arbitrary code before ECL can inspect anything; and d.9's `cached compiled form` still means threaded or opcode arrays only — a native extension is authored and compiled ahead of time by a person, not emitted by the runtime. Without this, a reader of d.21 alone would conclude native loading contradicts the positioning.

precedents.name: Sized-record / length-prefixed wire decoding with additive tails
precedents.whyApplicable: Vulkan's `sType`/`pNext` sized structs and protobuf's unknown-field rule are the working precedent for ABI major/minor with additive record tails: every record carries its own byte size, the reader takes `@min(declared, @sizeOf(local))`, and unknown trailing bytes are ignored rather than trusted. patches.title: Validate and copy descriptors through bounded cursors

files.description: The resumable descriptor validator and the runtime-owned `ValidatedDescriptor` it produces.
Export `native_descriptor` and add the new native test file to the aggregate test block.
Behavioural validator tests over host-owned backing buffers.
Add the native descriptor fuzz entry point.
Add the `fuzz-native-descriptor` campaign to the `fuzz_targets` table.
Classify `native_descriptor.zig` as native-component business logic and `tests/native_test.zig` as a test input.

changes: Create `src/native_descriptor.zig` with `pub const ValidatedDescriptor` — an opaque handle over runtime-owned storage holding the copied module `intern.NamespaceName`, the normalized module documentation, a definition table of `{ name: intern.NamespaceName, doc: *env.DocumentationString, effect: env.ValidatedEffect, callback_index: u32 }`, the copied capability requirement list, and the validated `StateLayout`. After validation it must borrow nothing from artifact memory; assert that by copying every byte through the existing `kernel_storage.TextMaterializer`/`doc.NormalizeCursor` path already used by `modules.Registry.nativeDocumentation` (modules.zig:1421).

Implement validation as a resumable `ValidateCursor` with a `pending | complete` progress union and a `advance(budget)` that polls, in the same shape as the existing cursors in modules.zig and reflection.zig. Phases: header size/version, module name, module doc, capability list, definition records, per-definition name/doc/effect, and finally the reserved state layout. Every read is bounded by `@min(declared_size, @sizeOf(local))` per `native/abi.zig`'s rule, and every count is multiplied against its record size with `std.math.mul` overflow checks before any pointer arithmetic.

Make the failure contract total and precise. Return a distinct, named error for each of: ABI major mismatch, unsupported capability id, unsupported capability version, descriptor or record size below the minimum, count/offset overflow, callback index >= callback table length, invalid UTF-8 in a name or documentation string, empty documentation after normalization, a name that `intern.internNamespace` rejects, an effect whose input/output names do not parse into `env.ValidatedEffect`, a duplicate definition name, a nonzero reserved state layout (module state is not a v1 capability), and a canonical module name different from the requested name. Each error carries the failing definition index where one applies. Add a `comptime` exhaustive switch that maps every `abi.ErrorKindWire` member onto its `machine.ErrorKind` counterpart, closing the direction Patch 1 asserted by name only.

Give the validator an explicit ownership contract on both paths: on success the caller receives one `ValidatedDescriptor` it must `deinit` through the Session's `heap.ReleaseDomain`; on any failure the cursor retires every partially materialized name, doc, and effect itself and the caller receives only the error. Do not read implementation source text; the descriptor bytes are a documented artifact contract, which is the one text input AGENTS.md permits.

changes: Create `src/native/sdk.zig` as the `ecl-native` module root. Its module-root directory is `src/native/`, so `@import("../machine.zig")` is a compile error — that directory boundary, not a denylist, is the enforcement that the SDK cannot reach interpreter internals. It may import only `abi.zig` and `capability.zig` from the same directory.

Implement `pub fn Call(comptime effect: []const u8) type`. Parse the effect at comptime into input and output name lists split on a single top-level `--`, rejecting a missing separator, an empty side name, a duplicate name, or a non-identifier slot with a `@compileError` naming the offending token. The generated type exposes `input(i)` returning a `ValueView` for `i < inputs.len`, `complete(tuple)` requiring `tuple.len == outputs.len`, `fail(kind, message)` restricted to `abi.ErrorKindWire`, and `forward(i)` producing a candidate that reuses input `i`. It exposes no allocator, no raw runtime value, and no stack operation.

Implement `pub fn word(name: []const u8, doc: []const u8, callback: anytype) Word` and `pub fn module(comptime spec: struct { name, doc, words }) type` which generates the descriptor, the per-definition `Invoke` thunks, and the single `export fn ecl_module_abi_v1(...)` entry point. Registration supplies only name, documentation, and callback — the effect, arity, and capability manifest are derived from the callback type so nothing can drift.

Implement the comptime reflection in one place. Over `@typeInfo(@TypeOf(callback))`, reject: a non-function, a generic or variadic function, a first parameter that is not `*Call(...)`, a return type that is not `error{OutOfMemory}!Outcome`, any later parameter that is not an exact SDK capability type, a duplicated capability, an empty documentation string, and a duplicate word name within the module. Emit the canonical capability requirement manifest (always `call`, plus one entry per named capability) so authors write no `.requires` list, callback symbol table, effect duplicate, or allocator plumbing.

Create `src/native/capability.zig` with exactly the capabilities this milestone can already exercise: `Outcome` (the opaque result of `complete`/`fail`), `ValueView` (immutable O(1) kind, scalar, and aggregate-length observation only — no backing slice, no iterator, no `Value`), `Scalar` constructors for int/float/char/symbol/word, and `BuildValues` for constructing list and dict candidates. `Reschedule` arrives in Patch 6 and completes the v1 set; `ModuleState`, `ModuleView`, and `ModuleUpdate` are deferred entirely, so an author naming them hits the reflection's unknown-capability rejection here and the validator's unsupported-capability rejection at load.

Its documentation strings are nonempty and its effects are the ones DoD-22 and DoD-23 assert.

It deliberately bypasses the SDK because the SDK rejects these shapes at comptime; that is the point.

In `build.zig` add a `test-native-sdk-negative` step that compiles each as an object with `expect_errors = .{ .contains = "<the SDK's exact message>" }` and depends on nothing else, so a rejection message change fails loudly.

This is the patch's proof that generation and validation agree.

files.description: The consuming load typestate, the module instance handle, image pinning, and Session-owned instance lifetime.
The native call transaction: pinned inputs, host-side `ValueView`/`BuildValues`, reserved-window commit, and non-completing rollback.
Add the `Binding.native` variant carrying a nominal `NativeCallable` and its module publication arm.
Dispatch `.native` bindings into the transaction and extend `AutoLoadDriver` with the `.eclmod` candidate.
Publish a validated descriptor's complete table through the existing candidate/commit protocol.
Own loaded native instances and order their teardown inside `deinit`.
Render native origin and capability requirements in `which` and `see`.
Export `native_module` and `native_call`.
Loader precedence, fail-closed, publication, reflection, and transaction atomicity proofs against the real fixture.
Release-binary discovery, ABI, and reflection acceptance.
Give `test/e2e.zig` the fixture output directory so the real binary can load it.
Classify `native_module.zig` and `native_call.zig` as native-component business logic.

changes: Create `src/native_module.zig` with the consuming typestate `Loading = union(enum) { opened, described, validated, initialized, published }`. Each variant owns exactly the `std.DynLib` handle, the copied `native_descriptor.ValidatedDescriptor`, and the rollback action valid in that phase. With module state deferred, `initialized` constructs the runtime instance from validated metadata; the host table remains an ephemeral invocation capability rather than an artifact-stored pointer. Every transition consumes one variant and constructs the next, and a failed transition cleans its own input. Model it on the existing `modules.OwnedCandidate`/`LoadingLease` capabilities rather than correlated raw fields.

Implement the platform boundary honestly. `opened` uses `std.DynLib.openZ` on the candidate path and `lookup(abi.EntryFn, abi.entry_symbol)`; on a target where `std.DynLib` is unsupported an existing `.eclmod` candidate is still authoritative and fails with a precise `'io` error naming the unsupported platform, never a silent fall-through. The load error message must state that opening a native library executes arbitrary trusted code before ECL can inspect the descriptor.

Introduce `pub const ModuleInstance = opaque {}` as the nominal per-Session instance handle. It owns the image pin, the validated descriptor, the callback table, and, when a future milestone adds module state, its storage. Expose only what a binding needs: `definitionCount`, `definition(index)`, `invoke(index)`, and `requirements()`. It exposes no `DynLib`, allocator, registry, environment, `Unit`, or reclamation domain, so the Session comptime authority sweep keeps passing.

Add `Binding.native: NativeCallable` to `src/env.zig`, where `NativeCallable = struct { instance: *native_module.ModuleInstance, definition: u32 }` — a nominal pair, never a raw callback/context pair. Add the matching `ModulePublication.native` arm carrying visibility, the validated effect, and documentation, and extend `BindingSpec.fromModule`, `Binding.retain`, and `Binding.retire` (native bindings retain the instance, not a heap value).

Reintroduce `modules.Registry.registerNative` with the descriptor-driven signature `pub fn registerNative(self: *Registry, instance: *native_module.ModuleInstance, descriptor: *const native_descriptor.ValidatedDescriptor) RegistryError!u64`. It calls the existing `createCandidate`, publishes every definition through `candidate.borrow().scope.publishModule` with `ModulePublication.native`, and commits with the existing `commit`, so publication stays atomic and a mid-table failure rolls the whole candidate back.

Extend `machine.AutoLoadDriver` (machine.zig:1818) so each `ECL_PATH` root produces two ordered candidates. Replace the single `.filename` phase (machine.zig:1875-1885, where `const extension = ".ecl";` is hard-coded) with a per-candidate suffix selector that builds `<name>.ecl` first and `<name>.eclmod` second inside the same root before advancing `search_index`. Keep the existing rule that `error.FileNotFound` moves to the next candidate and any other access error is authoritative. When the selected candidate is native, transfer to a new `NativeLoadDriver` instead of `fileSourceOwned`, consuming the same `LoadingLease` so recursive auto-load detection is unchanged.

Create `src/native_call.zig` implementing the transaction. On entry it requires the declared input count, pins those operands (they stay in place and immutable — nothing may pop them), and constructs the host side of `ValueView`, `forward`, and `BuildValues` as issuer-checked candidates owned by the transaction. Completion calls `Machine.reserveStack` (machine.zig:2612) for the exact final window *before* mutating anything, then atomically discards the inputs and pushes the declared outputs through the returned `StackReservation`. Failure, cancellation, deadline loss, OOM, and abandonment leave the operand stack byte-identical and transfer every candidate to `Machine.releaseDomain()` bounded retirement.

Restrict author error authority. A `fail` result maps its `abi.ErrorKindWire` onto the corresponding `machine.ErrorKind` and its bounded message into `machine.EclErr`; the runtime then attaches word, source, site, and trace exactly as it does for `.builtin` failures via `installPrimitiveFailure`. Underflow, undefined-word, contract, cancellation, timeout, and OOM are produced only by the runtime; an artifact cannot name them.

Replace the deleted `.primitive` arm in `machine.executeResolved` with a `.native => |callable|` arm that runs the cross-home effect check exactly as the `.builtin` arm does and then enters `native_call`. In this patch every native call completes within one dispatch; the `Reschedule` continuation arrives in Patch 6.

Make `Session` own loaded instances: a private list in `SessionCore`, populated by the loader under the existing `BlockingMutationTurn`, and torn down in `Session.deinit` after `core.scheduler.deinit(&core.root_tasks)` and before `core.registry.deinit()` — new native-call creation closes first, then instances release their pins. Add no public Session method that accepts or returns a descriptor, instance, or library handle.

Extend reflection in `src/definition_prims.zig`: `WhichDriver.initialize` renders a `.native` binding as `native` (where `.builtin` renders `primitive`) and appends ` requires <capability list>`; `SeeDriver.buildPlan` renders the body slot as `<native:<module>.<word>>` and keeps the ordinary combined `(effect : "doc")` annotation and `'<name> def` tail. `doc` needs no change — it already resolves the binding snapshot's documentation.

Add behavioural tests to `src/tests/native_test.zig` covering: atomic publication of the whole table with qualified, `use`d, and aliased access plus `words` visibility; a root holding both `sample.ecl` and `sample.eclmod` selecting the source candidate; two roots where the first holds only a native candidate and the second a source candidate, selecting the first; each malformed variant failing with its precise error while leaving `sample` absent from registry, `words`, and reflection and never selecting a later candidate; native reflection output; and a completing, a failing, and a cancelled call all leaving the expected operand stack. Add `e2e: native extension discovery ABI and reflection acceptance` to `test/e2e.zig` running the release binary against the installed fixture directory.

Give the `Loading` typestate two image-pin arms, `dynamic` (the `std.DynLib` handle) and `static` (a no-op pin over a comptime-known descriptor and callback table). Both arms traverse the identical `described -> validated -> initialized -> published` transitions, the identical `Registry.registerNative` publication, the identical transaction, and the identical shutdown order; only the pin differs. Expose the static entry as an internal function in `src/native_module.zig` taking an already-generated descriptor plus its callback table — never as a Session method, never accepting a raw library handle — so M10 registers CSV and JSON through it without any ECL-in-Zig embedding API appearing on `Session`.

Prove the static arm in this patch rather than shipping it unexercised: `src/tests/native_test.zig` already imports `test/native/sample.zig` as the `native-sample` Zig module (wired in Patch 3), so register that same fixture through the static transport and run the same publication, reflection, and transaction assertions the dynamically loaded artifact gets. Assert that both routes produce identical `doc`/`which`/`see` output apart from the origin's image kind.

In `build.zig`, add the fixture install directory to `e2e_options` so `test/e2e.zig` can point `ECL_PATH` at it, and make the e2e run depend on the `native-fixture` step. Append `native_module.zig` and `native_call.zig` to the native component in `src/tools/source_audit.zig` and export both from `src/root.zig`.

precedents.whyApplicable: Model `opened -> described -> validated -> initialized -> published` as a tagged union whose transition functions consume one variant and construct the next, exactly as `modules.OwnedCandidate` and `modules.LoadingLease` already do in this repo. patches.title: Make cooperation a typed Reschedule continuation on the production WorkDriver

files.description: Add `Reschedule(ContinuationSpec)`, the budget-charging aggregate cursors, and `consume`.
Accept and validate the reschedule capability and emit its wire requirement and adapter arm.
Add the reschedule host-callback entries and yield-state fields to the wire table.
Host-side continuation storage, budget accounting, cursor and builder implementations, and overrun diagnostics.
Add the opt-in `setNativeDiagnostics` mode switch.
Enable native diagnostics when ECL_NATIVE_DIAGNOSTICS is set.
Ordered native shutdown proof under the real scheduler.
Own aligned continuation storage, its library pin, and the ordered shutdown typestate.
Accept the reschedule capability id/version and validate the continuation state layout.
Add budget-spanning cooperative words used by the runtime and fuzz proofs.
Cooperative progress, budget charging, and yield-then-cancel atomicity proofs.
Add the native call transaction fuzz entry point.
Add the `fuzz-native-call` campaign and the native `test-tsan` filters.

changes: Add `pub fn Reschedule(comptime Spec: type) type` to `src/native/capability.zig`. `Spec` fixes the continuation's private Zig state type and an explicit bounded `deinit`. Comptime validation rejects a spec whose state recursively embeds a `Call`, a `ValueView`, any ephemeral capability, or a lifetime-incompatible handle, and rejects a spec with no destructor. The author gets `state()`, `yield()`, and `consume(n)`; there is no way to obtain the host allocator or the scheduler.

Give every aggregate access a metered cursor. `ValueView` keeps only O(1) kind, scalar, and aggregate-length observation; contents are reachable only through text, leaf, list, and dict cursors that charge the host budget per element, and `BuildValues` builders charge the same budget per appended element. There must be no raw backing slice and no unmetered iterator anywhere in the SDK surface — that absence is the contract, so state it in the doc comment and keep it true by construction rather than by review.

Extend `src/native/abi.zig` with the host-callback entries the cooperative path needs (charge budget, request yield, open/advance each cursor kind, append to each builder kind) and the yield-state fields, all as additive record tails under ABI major 1 per the negotiation rule Patch 1 froze. Bump `abi_minor`. Extend `src/native_descriptor.zig` to accept `capability.reschedule` at its supported version and to validate the declared continuation state size and alignment against the supported bounds.

In `src/native_call.zig`, make a rescheduling call install the real `machine.WorkDriver` through `Machine.installWorkDriver` from its *first* invocation, exactly like `AutoLoadDriver` and `UseDriver`. Each turn resets a 65,536-unit budget (`machine.kernel_poll_quantum`), calls `Machine.pollKernel` for cancellation, advances the callback once, and returns `.yielded` when the callback yields or the budget is exhausted. Inputs and candidate outputs stay pinned across the yield; `complete`/`fail`/`cancel` consumes the continuation exactly once and runs its bounded destructor exactly once. Teardown on cancellation or OOM goes through the driver's `destroy`, so the continuation cannot outlive the reclamation domain.

Let `native_module.ModuleInstance` own the aligned opaque continuation storage and hold the library pin for the continuation's whole life, so a delayed continuation keeps the image alive independently of the binding that started it.

Now that continuations exist, make Session shutdown explicitly close new native-call creation, join and cancel outstanding tasks, destroy every call continuation, settle ECL retirement, and only then release registry-held image pins. `Session.deinit` drives that owner protocol. all art: Artifact, builds art | module-count art = 1.
all art: Artifact, builds art | entry-points art = 1.

> Bindings are word, value, builtin, or native; the old general-stack seam is
> gone in every form.
all bd: Binding | kind bd = word-kind or kind bd = value-kind or kind bd = builtin-kind
    or kind bd = native-kind.
all cb: Callback, general-stack cb | reachable cb = false.
all reg: Registration, host-registration reg | available reg = false.

> Resolution is ordered, source-first inside a root, and fails closed.
all rt: Root, exists rt source-candidate | selected rt = source-candidate.
all rt: Root, exists rt source-candidate = false, exists rt native-candidate |
    selected rt = native-candidate.
all m: Module, i: Nat0, i < candidate-root m | exists (root i) source-candidate = false.
all m: Module, i: Nat0, i < candidate-root m | exists (root i) native-candidate = false.
all m: Module, loads m = false | published m = false.
all m: Module, loads m = false | visible m = false.
all m: Module, loads m = false | reflects m = false.
all m: Module | visible m = published m.
all m: Module, published m | reflects m.
all m: Module, published m | pinned-image (instance m).

> Loading is a consuming typestate in one fixed order.
load-order opened < load-order described.
load-order described < load-order validated-phase.
load-order validated-phase < load-order initialized.
load-order initialized < load-order published-phase.
all m: Module, published m | reached m initialized.

> Calls are transactional leaves over immutable inputs.
all cl: Call | inputs-immutable cl.
all cl: Call | depth (after cl) = cond
    result cl = complete-result => depth (before cl) - inputs cl + declared-outputs cl,
    true => depth (before cl).
all cl: Call, result cl = fail-result | retired cl.
all cl: Call, result cl = cancel-result | retired cl.
all cl: Call, result cl = oom-result | retired cl.
all cl: Call, result cl = fail-result | author-kind (raised cl).

> Cooperation is metered, resumable, consumed once, and never preemptive.
all cont: Continuation, i: Nat0, scheduler-attached cont | charged (slice-of cont i) <= quantum.
all cont: Continuation, i: Nat0, yields (slice-of cont i) | preserved cont.
all cont: Continuation, i: Nat0, yields (slice-of cont i) | inputs-pinned cont.
all cont: Continuation, i: Nat0, yields (slice-of cont i) | builders-preserved cont.
all cont: Continuation, i: Nat0 | turn-drafts-retired (slice-of cont i).
all cu: Cursor | charged-by cu = observed cu.
all cu: Cursor | unmetered cu = false.
all cont: Continuation, terminal cont | consumptions cont = 1.
all cont: Continuation, terminal cont | destructor-runs cont = 1.
all u: Unit, cont: Continuation, ready u, scheduler-attached cont | advances u cont.
all cont: Continuation, i: Nat0, diagnostics-enabled, over-quantum (slice-of cont i) |
    overrun-reported (slice-of cont i).
all cont: Continuation, i: Nat0, diagnostics-enabled = false |
    overrun-reported (slice-of cont i) = false.
all cont: Continuation, i: Nat0 | preempts (slice-of cont i) = false.

> Shutdown runs each phase exactly once in the fixed order.
shutdown-order close-calls < shutdown-order destroy-continuations.
shutdown-order destroy-continuations < shutdown-order settle-retirement.
shutdown-order settle-retirement < shutdown-order close-image.
all sd: Shutdown, sp: ShutdownPhase | runs sd sp = 1.

> Acceptance is worker-count invariant, bounded, blocking, budgeted, documented.
all wa: WorkerCount, wb: WorkerCount | stdout (execute wa) = stdout (execute wb).
all wa: WorkerCount, wb: WorkerCount | status (execute wa) = status (execute wb).
all wc: WorkerCount | retired-bytes (execute wc) <= baseline-bytes (execute wc).
all i: Nat0, i < gate-count | blocking (native-gate i).
all comp: Component | measured comp <= ceiling comp.
all comp: Component | measured comp <= total-ceiling.
